Augment a fitted nnet model with statistical summaries

Source: R/statnnet.R
statnnet.Rd

statnnet() adds covariance estimates, Wald summaries, and covariate-effect calculations to a supported model fitted by nnet::nnet(). The original fit is retained. A model selected by select_nnet() can also be supplied.

Usage

statnnet(object, ...)

# Default S3 method
statnnet(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'statnnet_selection'
statnnet(object, covariance_tol = 1e-10, objective_tol = 1e-06, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nnet'
statnnet(
  object,
  formula = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  response = NULL,
  covariance_tol = 1e-10,
  objective_tol = 1e-06,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted object inheriting from "nnet", or a "statnnet_selection" object returned by select_nnet().

...

Reserved for methods.

covariance_tol

Relative numerical tolerance used to decide whether the penalised information matrix is reliably invertible.

objective_tol

Relative tolerance for validating the reconstructed fitting criterion against object$value.

formula

The formula used to fit object. This may be omitted for an nnet.formula object.

data

The original training data.

response

Either "continuous" or "binary". When NULL, the response type is inferred from the fitted nnet object.

Value

An object of class "statnnet" containing the original fit, reconstructed model information, covariance calculations, and diagnostics.

Details

Covariance calculations are returned only when the fitted Hessian passes the numerical checks. Wald tests and delta-method intervals are still approximations conditional on the fitted architecture and local solution. A warning is given when the hidden layer is larger than the fitted input layer. Binary-response summaries should be treated as exploratory because their frequentist calibration has not been studied by the package authors.

Examples

data("auto_mpg", package = "statnnet")
example_data <- auto_mpg
example_data$mpg <- as.numeric(scale(example_data$mpg))
example_data$weight <- as.numeric(scale(example_data$weight))
set.seed(3)
fit <- nnet::nnet(
  mpg ~ weight + origin,
  data = example_data,
  size = 1,
  linout = TRUE,
  decay = 0.1,
  Hess = TRUE,
  maxit = 500,
  trace = FALSE
)
model <- statnnet(fit, data = example_data, response = "continuous")
model
#> statnnet: statistical summary of a fitted nnet model
#> Formula: mpg ~ weight + origin
#> Architecture: 3-1-1; 6 weights; n = 392
#> Response: continuous; decay: 0.1
#> nnet convergence code: 0
#> Covariance: available (reciprocal condition number 0.000415)
